newsitem.title: USA: IMF approves resumed payments to Russia.
newsitem.headline: IMF approves resumed payments to Russia.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund agreed to resume lending to Russia after completing a review of the state of the Russian economy and approved the release of almost $700 million, an IMF official said on Friday.
The IMF's board, which is backing Russian reforms with a $10 billion three-year loan, met on Friday to assess the Russian Federation's program under terms for its Extended Fund Facility (EFF) loan.

"On the basis of understandings reached on the macroeconomic and structural policies for 1997, and recent actions to bolster revenue performance and implement a suitably prudent budget in 1997 ... the executive directors approved the 1997 program with total commitments of $2.8 billion and the first quarterly disbursement of $696.7 million under that program," the official said in a statement.

The IMF, which assessed Russia's economic performance each month under the first year of the three-year loan, delayed several monthly payments this year and last year because it was worried about Moscow's ability to raise tax revenue.
But officials agreed to switch to quarterly monitoring this year and the release of the funds on Friday represented the first quarterly tranche of the 1997 program.
The IMF statement gave no other details on the board's decision.
The IMF has forecast that Russia's economy will at last start to grow this year, with gross domestic product rising 2.8 percent, while inflation will slow to a post-reform low of 14 percent.
